evidence: All 6 production modules are small (avg ~47 LOC) with a single layer between CLI (lev/cli.py), orchestration (lev/loop.py), engine (lev/engine.py), and typed domain models (lev/types.py); no helper chains or wrapper hops exist anywhere.
lev/router.py converts untyped JSON dicts into frozen dataclasses at a single obvious boundary; no dict/config parameter bags leak past the boundary into engine or loop logic.
No Protocols, ABCs, single-implementation interfaces, *args/**kwargs forwarders, or generic utils modules exist; all engine functions operate directly on concrete Counter/dict types.
lev/__init__.py is an intentional 13-line public facade with __all__ (skip-listed), and the mechanical facade flags on loop.py/cli.py are import-driven false positives, not re-export surfaces.
Only minor indirection: engine.confidence() is a one-line wrapper around max(dist.values()) used at 3 call sites, a domain alias whose value is borderline.
abstraction_fitness.issues_preventing_higher_score: engine.confidence() is a thin pass-through alias for max(dist.values()) — the only layer of indirection in the codebase that does not clearly pay for itself; removing or inlining it is a judgment call.

abstraction_fitness.dimension_character: This is a small, flat, deliberately direct codebase: four frozen dataclasses in types.py, a pure-function engine, one orchestration loop, a JSON-to-model router, and a CLI. Every layer maps to a domain responsibility and abstractions are concrete — there are no protocols, generic helper modules, kwargs forwarders, or implicit parameter bags; dicts are converted to typed models at exactly one boundary (router.py). The single mechanical 'wrapper' signals (confidence, tokenize) are domain-named one-liners, not indirection chains.
abstraction_fitness.score_rationale: Against the global anchors this sits between strong (90) and exemplary (100): a developer benefits from essentially every layer and navigates from CLI to engine in one hop. The only cost is confidence() being a borderline alias for max(dist.values()) plus the mechanical facade flags on loop.py/cli.py which are import-driven false positives. Nothing here slows a developer down materially, keeping the score in the mid-90s rather than 100.

issues.summary: engine.confidence() is a pass-through one-liner wrapping max(dist.values()) with no policy or translation
evidence: lev/engine.py: confidence() body is exactly `return max(dist.values())` with no validation, scaling, or other logic
The name adds domain vocabulary over max(), but at 3 trivial call sites (all in loop.py) the indirection does not pay for itself
issues.suggestion: Either inline max(dist.values()) at the loop.py call sites, or keep confidence() only if the project intends to evolve it (e.g. margin-based confidence); if kept, add a brief docstring stating it is the deliberate confidence contract so future readers do not treat it as dead indirection.
